parsed.summary: The file proves three things. First, a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, has ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3-1/48)}, given as e(G)^16 ≤ C·n^21 for every F-free host and every n, and also in IsBigO form. Second, each member F ∈ F satisfies ex(n,F) ≥ c·n^{4/3} for all large n. Third, F is not compact, and the corrected Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture (∀ nonempty finite cyclic family ∃ F, C>0 with ex(n,F) ≤ C·ex(n,F) eventually) is false. The definitions match the paper's notions; the only caveats are harmless padding conjuncts (pure arithmetic facts) and a bound that is slightly stronger than the paper's (it holds for all n).

glossary.plain: A finite simple graph on vertex set Fin order.
The host contains no member of the family as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph.
glossary.note: SimpleGraph.Free means there is no subgraph copy, which matches the paper's definition.

glossary.plain: ex(n,F) = max |E(G)| over F-free G on n vertices, with sup ∅ = 0.
glossary.note: The filter is never empty for cyclic families, since the empty graph is free.

glossary.plain: ∃ F ∈ F, ∃ C>0, eventually ex(n,F) ≤ C·ex(n,F).
Every finite nonempty family whose members all contain cycles is compact.
For every F ∈ F, eventually c·n^{4/3} ≤ ex(n,F).
glossary.note: A single constant c for all members is equivalent to separate constants because the family is finite.

lean_claims.plain: The compactness conjecture, as defined, is false.

There exist a nonempty finite family F of connected, bipartite, non-acyclic graphs and constants c>0, C≥0 such that: (a) for each F ∈ F, eventually c n^{4/3} ≤ ex(n,F); (b) for all n and all F-free G on n vertices, e(G)^16 ≤ C n^21; (c) ex(n,F)^16 ≤ C n^21 for all n; (d) the trivial facts 0 < 1/48 and 21/16 = 4/3 - 1/48; (e) F is not compact; (f) the conjecture is false.

There exist a nonempty finite family F of connected, bipartite, cyclic graphs and c>0 such that each member has ex(n,F) ≥ c n^{4/3} eventually, ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3-1/48}) as n→∞, F is not compact, and the conjecture is false.

paper_claims.plain: There is a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3-1/48}) and ex(n,F) = Ω(n^{4/3}) for each F ∈ F; in particular no member satisfies (1), disproving the compactness conjecture.
There is a connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H with ex(n,H) ≥ c n^{3/2+ε} for all large n.

coverage.why: Same family properties, the same O bound and the same Ω bound, plus non-compactness.
The upper bound holds for all n and all hosts with an explicit constant.
Negation of the faithfully formalized corrected conjecture (1).

flags.explanation: The conjuncts 0<1/48 and 21/16 = 4/3-1/48 are pure arithmetic padding. They are true and harmless; they only document that the exponent 21/16 equals 4/3-ε.
The upper bound is stated for all n, including n=0, rather than asymptotically. This is stronger than the paper's O-bound, which is fine.

lint_verdicts.why: edgeFinset of a graph on Fin n is a genuine finite cardinality.
Real division of nonzero literals; 4/3 is exact.
Edge count of a finite graph; no infinite-type card is involved.
Real exponent 4/3 - 1/48 with nonzero literal denominators.
